findings.title: Power log capture hit its byte bound without covering the source window.
findings.evidence: size_limit, log_brackets_window=false, zero in-window timestamp rows and one malformed timestamp row.
findings.interpretation: The capture bound worked, but historical correlation is unavailable in this report. events_truncated=false refers only to the 256 recognized-event cap; it does not mean the raw capture was complete. The malformed row may be a cut line or another parsing problem; no raw log was transferred to decide.
findings.disposition: Preserve the failed ZIP. Do not raise bounds or repeat collection automatically. Continue with prospective continuity instrumentation before another acceptance experiment.

findings.title: Historical UTC/monotonic discrepancy remains unexplained.
findings.evidence: 15767.860335 UTC seconds versus 1593.0425461659906 monotonic seconds; current host reports Python 3.14.3 and mach_absolute_time() for monotonic/perf_counter.
findings.interpretation: Current metadata does not identify the historical interpreter or distinguish sleep, clock adjustment or another timing issue. Zero exported sleep events does not prove no sleep.
findings.disposition: Keep cause_confirmed=false and avoid historical throughput or latency conclusions. Require both clocks, per-operation measurements and a supervised awake guard in the next version.

findings.title: The historical PostgreSQL peak still fails the frozen memory predicate.
findings.evidence: Source events-memory-v1 remains failed; this follow-up makes no new memory observation.
findings.disposition: No resource increase, counter reset, reinterpretation or promotion. A separately versioned prospective operational criterion remains to be implemented and tested.

interpreter_comparison.reason: Source environment records commit and hashes but no Python version or executable identity. Current Python 3.14.3 does not establish the historical interpreter.

declared_by_mac24_not_independently_repr.scope: 131 host tests, before/after local source preservation and execution scope are mac24 declarations. The main Mac verified received archive/source bytes and code, but did not inspect the physical host, rerun its tests or receive raw power logs.

limits: Incomplete historical capture is accepted as valid failure evidence, not as successful collection or completed T5.
No raw power log was transferred; observed counts and capture status cannot be independently regenerated from the original host log here.
The frozen source lacks historical Python/executable identity. No inference that the interpreter changed or stayed the same is justified.
Prospective clock controls and the proposed memory criterion are not integrated into events-check. Historical failed reports remain unchanged.
No new mac24 execution is pending from receipt of this evidence; T6-T8 and final quality acceptance remain pending.

next_step.action: Implement and verify a separately versioned T5 operational protocol with prospective continuity evidence.
sequence: Integrate the existing Timeline and supervised AwakeGuard; record current clock metadata and UTC/monotonic start/end marks around seed, captures, each HTTP operation and restart. Preserve observations and a structured failure on discontinuity.
Apply the predeclared 2-second continuity tolerance and 7200-second budget; pass remaining time to bounded subprocess/HTTP operations. A suspended host can only detect failure after resuming.

Version acceptance explicitly: retain exact resource limits, no captured swap/OOM, complete functional replay, source integrity and expected generations. Preserve lifetime peak/max/pressure as diagnostics under the proposed new contract; keep both historical validators unchanged. Load/headroom remain T8.

Validate code and failure reporting with local synthetic and appropriate host/integration checks, then issue one exact-commit mac24 prompt for H&M. No automatic collection retry, old-protocol replay, training, test or T6.
